name: Tsuyosa Automatic
alt: Citizen Tsuyosa NJ0150-56X with green dial and stainless steel bracelet
label: For your first automatic
intro: A little color. A lot of character.
why: The green dial and integrated bracelet give this three-hand watch a distinct personality. Consider it if you want a mechanical watch that can move from a workday to dinner without changing straps.
tradeoff: An automatic needs regular wear or winding. Choose a quartz or light-powered watch if you want to pick it up after weeks in a drawer and go.

name: Marlin Chronograph
alt: Timex Marlin chronograph with silver dial, dark subdials and steel bracelet
label: For the vintage look
intro: The charm of a different decade.
why: A silver dial, dark subdials and a domed crystal give the Marlin a vintage-inspired look. The quartz chronograph offers stopwatch functionality without the winding routine of a mechanical movement.
tradeoff: The acrylic crystal is part of the retro appeal, but it needs more care around scratches than sapphire. Check the model number: Marlin variants use different straps and movements.

name: Brycen Eco-Drive
alt: Citizen Brycen chronograph with ivory dial and brown leather strap
label: For a bigger presence
intro: A weekend watch with useful details.
why: The ivory dial, dark bezel and brown leather strap create a relaxed, sporty combination. Eco-Drive uses light to charge the watch, while a chronograph adds elapsed-time measurement.
tradeoff: At 44 mm, this is the largest watch in our starter selection. Compare the size with a watch you already wear, and consider whether you prefer a leather strap or bracelet.

name: F-91W Digital
alt: Casio F-91W-1 watch, manufacturer product view
label: For a light everyday watch
why: A slim resin case and digital display make the F-91W a practical starting point for someone who wants time, an alarm and a stopwatch without a charging routine. At 21 grams, it also makes sense if you dislike a heavy watch.
tradeoff: The basic water-resistance rating is a reason to look elsewhere for swimming. Its resin glass also calls for care around scratches.

name: AE-1200 World Time
alt: Casio AE-1200WHD-1AV watch, manufacturer product view
label: For time across time zones
intro: A small world on your wrist.
why: World time, five alarms and a countdown timer give this digital watch a useful travel toolkit. Choose the steel-bracelet version if you like the silver look and want more wrist presence than the F-91W.
tradeoff: The bracelet is steel, but the case and glass are resin. Its busy display and multiple modes suit someone willing to learn the controls.
popularityNote: Included on Casio’s US Best Sellers page, checked October 13, 2026. The page retains a 2025 heading; this is not a verified current sales rank.

name: GA-2100 Blackout
alt: G-Shock GA-2100-1A1 watch, manufacturer product view
label: For an active routine
why: The all-black GA-2100 combines analog hands with digital tools in a shock-resistant case. Its 11.8 mm thickness is worth considering if you want a sports watch without an especially tall profile.
tradeoff: The dark hands and markers prioritize the monochrome look; consider a contrasting dial if quick readability matters most. This model uses batteries rather than solar charging.
facts: World time, alarms and countdown timer
popularityNote: Included on Casio’s US Best Sellers page, checked October 13, 2026. The page retains a 2025 heading; this is not a verified current sales rank.

name: 5 Sports Blue Dial
alt: Seiko SRPD51 watch, manufacturer product view
label: For a sporty automatic
why: The SRPD51 brings together a blue sunray dial, rotating bezel and day/date display. Its automatic movement and exhibition caseback make it an appealing introduction to mechanical watches with a sporty appearance.
tradeoff: At 13.4 mm thick, it deserves a fit check under a cuff. Expect to reset it after time unworn: the stated power reserve is approximately 41 hours.
popularityNote: Included in Seiko USA’s Best Sellers collection, checked October 13, 2026.

name: 5 Sports Field
alt: Seiko SRPJ85 watch, manufacturer product view
label: For a smaller mechanical watch
why: A black dial, beige numerals and olive nylon strap give the SRPJ85 a casual field-watch character. The 36.4 mm diameter offers a smaller alternative to the larger sports watches in this collection.
tradeoff: A smaller diameter does not mean an ultra-thin watch: the case is 12.5 mm thick. Like the SRPD51, its automatic movement needs wear or winding and can stop after roughly 41 hours.
popularityNote: Included in Seiko USA’s Best Sellers collection, checked October 13, 2026.
